skill.name: simplify
skill.description: Simplify and refine recently modified code for clarity and consistency. Use after writing code to improve readability without changing functionality.
skill.summary: Refines recently changed code for clarity, consistency, and maintainability without changing behavior.
skill.author: brianlovin

content.value_statement: Code changes often leave behind duplicated logic, inconsistent style, or confusing structure. This skill reviews recently modified code and refines it for clarity while preserving behavior.
actual_capabilities: Reviews recently modified code for unnecessary complexity, nesting, and redundancy.
Applies project standards such as import sorting, explicit types, and React Props patterns.
Improves variable and function names when clearer names improve maintainability.
Consolidates related logic while preserving features, outputs, and behavior.
Documents only significant changes that affect understanding.
limitations: It relies on surrounding project standards being available and accurate.
It does not replace tests or formal regression verification.
It focuses on recently touched code unless the user requests broader review.
It may avoid changes when simplification would reduce clarity.

use_cases.title: Clean Up UI Changes
use_cases.description: Refine recently edited React components for clearer props, simpler branches, and consistent project style.

use_cases.title: Prepare Refactors For Review
use_cases.description: Reduce redundant logic and improve names before sending a pull request for human review.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Code
use_cases.description: Apply local readability and maintainability rules to touched files without changing behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Simplify My Recent Changes
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner cleanup after a small edit
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the simplify skill on the files I just changed. Preserve behavior and tell me only the meaningful refinements.

prompt_templates.title: Apply Project Style
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my touched code against the project standards. Improve clarity, naming, imports, and type annotations without changing outputs.

prompt_templates.title: Refine React Components
prompt_templates.prompt: Simplify the React components I edited. Keep explicit Props types, improve conditional rendering, and remove comments that only repeat the code.

prompt_templates.title: Constrain A Broad Refactor
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of a larger change
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect the recent refactor for over-abstraction, nested logic, and unclear names. Make targeted simplifications, then summarize remaining tradeoffs.

output_examples.input: A recently edited React component mixes nested conditions, inconsistent prop names, and redundant comments.
output_examples.output: Simplified the condition handling, aligned prop names with the component API, and removed comments that repeated visible behavior.

output_examples.input: A service function has repeated validation branches and unclear temporary names.
output_examples.output: Consolidated the shared validation flow, renamed temporary values for intent, and preserved each original error case.

output_examples.input: A pull request touched import order, type annotations, and small helper functions.
output_examples.output: Sorted imports, added explicit top-level return types, and kept helper functions separate where that improved readability.

best_practices: Run the skill after implementation, before final tests and review.
Keep the requested scope close to files changed in the current session.
Review behavior-sensitive changes with tests after simplification.
anti_patterns: Do not ask it to minimize line count as the main goal.
Do not use it to rewrite unrelated areas without a clear scope.
Do not accept simplifications that remove useful abstractions or context.

faq.question: Does this skill change program behavior?
faq.answer: It is designed to preserve existing behavior and improve only structure, naming, consistency, and readability.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it after writing or modifying code, before final review or regression testing.

faq.question: Can it review an entire codebase?
faq.answer: Its default scope is recently modified code. Ask for a broader scope only when that review is intentional.

faq.question: Does it work with TypeScript and React?
faq.answer: Yes. The instructions mention TypeScript return types, ES modules, and React component Props patterns.

faq.question: Will it remove comments?
faq.answer: It may remove comments that describe obvious code, but should keep comments that explain important intent.

faq.question: Does it replace tests?
faq.answer: No. Run tests after simplification when behavior must be verified.
